sub: Nearly 2,000 years ago, in the Pandya kingdom of Madurai, a boy was crowned king.
His name was Nedunchezhiyan. He was still a teenager.
Beyond his borders, the kings laughed. “A mere boy,” they said.
The Chera king. The Chola king. Five chieftains beside them. Seven armies, joined as one.
The young king made a vow: “If I do not crush them, let no poet ever sing my name.”
He marched out to meet them at Thalaiyalanganam.
And there, the boy they had mocked shattered the entire alliance.
The poets have sung his name ever since.
